Earlier this year, Apple raised prices significantly due to the global memory crisis. The iPad Air jumped from $599 to $749, the M5 MacBook Pro from $1,699 to $1,999, and the Apple TV from $129 to $199. The above are just some examples—the key point is that these price hikes were quite staggering.

This situation inevitably raises the question—will Apple make major improvements to its products to keep them appealing at the new price points?

Of course, some Apple products are about to receive major updates, with the MacBook Pro and iPad mini being two such examples. However, for products that won't see significant changes in the near term, I really can't imagine how Apple can charge a premium for "yesterday's technology" while still making consumers feel it's worth buying—especially when compared to current second-hand market prices.

If just a few months ago you could buy an M4 iPad Air for $599 (or even as low as $499), why pay $749 now? This logic becomes even more apparent when applied to higher-priced products.

Some Apple products haven't seen major changes in a long time. The iPad Air has used the same design and feature set since 2020, with only chip upgrades and Apple Pencil Pro support added along the way. The basic iPad has largely remained unchanged since 2022, and the iMac has stayed more or less the same from 2021 to now.

Do these products need a redesign? Not necessarily. But I think Apple could do something to make them more attractive at their current price points. For example, giving the iMac a miniLED display, upgrading the iPad Air to 120Hz, or giving the basic iPad a fully laminated display.

Compared to the magnitude of the price hikes, the cost of these upgrades is relatively low, but they could likely make consumers feel better about the new pricing. On the other hand, Apple might also downgrade some product specifications to offset pricing pressures—for instance, the iPhone could see the return of a 128GB storage option at any time.

What are your thoughts on Apple's product lineup after the price hikes? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
